APPROVAL OF MINUTES
  EL MONTE CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING
  OF NOVEMBER 4, 2020

MEETING JOINTLY AND REGULARLY WITH THE EL MONTE HOUSING AUTHORITY; EL
MONTE PUBLIC FINANCING AUTHORITY; EL MONTE WATER AUTHORITY; EL MONTE
PARKING AUTHORITY; SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE FORMER EL MONTE COMMUNITY
REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY; HOUSING SUCCESSOR AGENCY; AND, FROM TIME TO
TIME, SUCH OTHER BODIES OF THE CITY WHOSE MEMBERSHIP IS COMPOSED
EXCLUSIVELY OF THE MEMBERSHIP OF THE CITY COUNCIL

1.  CALL TO ORDER: 6:04 p.m.

2.  ROLL CALL FOR CITY COUNCIL AND AUTHORITY BODIES:

  Andre Quintero, Mayor/Chair – present
  Maria Morales, Mayor Pro Tem/Authority Member – present
  Jessica Ancona, Councilmember/Authority Member – present
  Victoria Martinez Muela, Councilmember/Authority Member – present
  Jerry Velasco, Councilmember/Authority Member – present

3.  APPROVAL OF AGENDA:

  m) Mayor Quintero
  s) Councilmember Velasco  5-0

4.  CLOSED SESSION (6:00 p.m. – 7:00 p.m.):

  The City Council and the various Authority Bodies whose membership is composed
  exclusively of the membership of the City Council (collectively, the “Council”) will attempt
  to address and complete all Closed Session business between 6:00 p.m. and 7:00 p.m.
  If the Council completes all Closed Session business prior to 7:00 p.m., the Council will
  take a short recess and commence all Open Session proceedings promptly at 7:00 p.m.
  In the event the City Council is unable to address or complete all agendized Closed
  Session items by 7:00 p.m., the Council will hear all such remaining items toward the
  end of the meeting, immediately following Council Communications. Should any member
  of the public wish to address the Council on any agendized Closed Session matter, the
  Council shall allow such person to address the Council on such matter prior to going into
  Closed Session, provided that all persons wishing to address the Council on an
  agendized Closed Session matter shall fill out a speaker card and be subject to a
  speaker’s time limit of 3 minutes per speaker and further provided that the Council shall
  be under no obligation to respond to or deliberate upon any specific questions or
  comments posed by a speaker or take action on any issue raised by a speaker beyond
  such action as the City Council may be lawfully authorized to take on an agendized
  Closed Session matter pursuant to the Brown Act (Govt. Code Section 54950 et seq.).
   City Council Meeting Minutes of November 4, 2020

  Mayor Quintero and the City Council recessed into Closed Session at

  Closed Session at approximately 7:01 pm.

  Assistant City Attorney Richard Padilla reported out of Closed Session with

8.  PUBLIC COMMENT REGARDING NON-AGENDIZED MATTERS:

  This time has been set aside for persons in the audience to make comments or inquiries
  on matters within the general subject matter jurisdiction of the City Council, the Housing
  Authority, the Financing Authority and/or the Water Authority (collectively, the “Council”)
  that are not listed on this agenda. Although no person is required to provide their
  name and address as a condition to attending a Council meeting, persons who wish to
  address the Council are asked to state their name and address. Each speaker will be
  limited to three (3) continuous minutes. Speakers may not lend any portion of their
  speaking time to other persons or borrow additional time from other persons.

  Except as otherwise provided under the Brown Act (Gov. Code Section 54950 et seq.),
  the Council may not deliberate or take action upon any matter not listed on this posted
  agenda but may order that any such matter be placed on the agenda for a subsequent
  meeting. The Council may also direct staff to investigate certain matters for
  consideration at a future meeting.

  All comments or queries presented by a speaker shall be addressed to the Council as a
  body and not to any specific member thereof. No questions shall be posed to any
  member of the Council except through the presiding official of the meeting, the Mayor
  and/or Chair. Members of the Council are under no obligation to respond to questions
  posed by speakers but may provide brief clarifying responses to any comment made or
  questions posed. The Council may not engage in any sort of prolonged discussion or
  deliberation with any speaker or group of speakers on matters that are not listed on this
  agenda.

  Enforcement of Decorum: The Chief of Police, or such member, or members of the
  Police Department as the Chief of Police may designate, shall serve as the Sergeant-at-
  Arms of any Council meeting. The Sergeant-at-Arms shall carry out all orders and
  instructions given by the presiding official for the purpose of maintaining order and
  decorum at the meeting. While members of the public are free to level criticism of City
  policies and the action(s) or proposed action(s) of the Council or its members, members
  of the public may not engage in behavior that is disruptive to the orderly conduct of the
  proceedings, including, but not limited to, conduct that prevents other members of the
  3
   City Council Meeting Minutes of November 4, 2020

  public from being heard when it is their opportunity to speak or which prevents members
  of the audience from hearing or seeing the proceedings. Members of the public may not
  threaten any person with physical harm or act in a manner that may reasonably be
  interpreted as an imminent threat of physical harm. All persons attending the meeting
  must adhere to the City’s policy barring harassment based upon a person’s race,
  religious creed, color, national origin, ancestry, physical handicap, medical condition,
  marital status, gender, sexual orientation or age.

  Councilmember Martinez Muela – I hope we are able to address anyone waiting in
  public comment particularly Mr. Gabriel Ramirez. My message today is one of gratitude
  to Councilwoman Morales for the phone call today, for City Manager Martinez for her
  phone call today and from Alma Puente for her phone call today. I appreciate the reach
  outs today it has been a tremendous day of communication and the potential
  conversation for building bridges I appreciate that and I wanted to just say thank you. It
  is an opportunity for our City to start moving forward it is exciting. My other message for
  today is one of sadness because there is an emptiness here at City Hall and while we
  are going to be adjourning later on today I couldn’t not speak to the incredible man for
  me that Dave Gondek was. Forgive my emotion but this is the kind of man that will take
  as much time as it takes for you to understand an issue. This was a man that was a
  great friend, a mentor, a legal legal and someone who would drive you crazy with his
  long drawn out descriptions of sometimes simple ideas. He was an El Monte institution.
  He will be missed walking into Council Chambers today and moving forward. I just didn’t
  want to miss out on the opportunity to say thank you Dave Gondek for your years of
  service to this community for your years of love to the City of El Monte.

18.  COUNCIL COMMUNICATIONS/REPORTS:

  18A.  Mayor Quintero

  18B.  Mayor Pro Tem Morales

  My condolences to the Gondek family and to OMLO as a firm. I know that a
  good number of our staff members worked for many many years with Mr.
  Gondek and for the two years, actually four years because I did work with him
  from time to time on the Planning Commission. You can tell there was a lot of
  institutional knowledge that is no longer going to be here. He definitely knew the
  ins and outs of what was occurring in the City and during that short period I
  learned a tremendous deal from him particularly his love for this community and
  the fact that he really cared my condolences to his family and to our staff who
  worked very closely with him and he will be definitely be missed. I wanted to say
  thank you to the community we had a great opening for the skate park I know it is
  an awkward transition to go from condolences to a celebration but frankly these
  days have been more than just challenging for our community given COVID,
  given the restrictions of social distancing, just the elections that occurred
  yesterday and the fact that many of these places are still undecided so there has
  been a lot going on and our community is going through a lot. To our staff I want
  to say thank you because given all of those changes and adjustments and the
  pivoting that has been happening since March you are constantly and precisely
  devoted to the work that you do and it is highly noted and I thank you for all the
  work that goes into making sure that the rules of government continue even while
  there is a transition so I thank you for all of your work. To the community we
  have to continue to move forward and continue to stay focused on improving an
  overall community long term.

  18C.  Councilwoman Ancona

  Back in August we discussed a hiring and promotion freeze and I want to make
  sure that that is still in effect at this time and that we are not hiring or promoting
  any employees in the City of El Monte due to our budget constraints. I would like
  to ask staff to start considering let’s look at what other cities are doing in regards
  to allowing the public to come in and be able to speak to certain items whether
  we have maybe social distance outside and let them in. I see we have some
  rows that are cautioned taped off we have allowed other members to come in
  and speak at these meetings so I would like to start looking into ways that we can
  start allowing some of the public back in in small numbers with property protocols
  and procedures. And lastly, my condolences to the Gondek family and the
  OMLO family. I only got to work with Dave for a couple of years but the news
  was impactful and if that is how I felt after two years of working with him I can
  only imagine the loss felt by everybody else.

  18D.  Councilwoman Martinez Muela

  I am going to hold over my council communications to the next meeting for today
  I think it has been a trying couple of months and I think everyone can get home
  early it would be a great thing. So thank you very much for the time and thank
  you for just allowing me the opportunity to be your Councilwoman I am
  appreciative of all of the relationships that we have built all the time, effort and
  energy that we put toward moving El Monte into a positive and fuller space. So
  thank you staff, thank you community and thank you for the time tonight and
  thank you for closing in honor of Dave Gondek.

  18D.1 Discussion Regarding State Audit.

  18D.2 Discussion Regarding Transparency in Financial Management Policy.

  18E.  Councilman Velasco

  I will give a report at the next meeting on the Census and Cathi Eredia did a
  great work and all the people, NALEO and all the other organizations that have
  worked with you. Our numbers went really high you guys worked really hard City
  of El Monte is being recognized by a lot of other institutions and other cities for
  being so involved and bringing lots of people to make sure that our residents are
  counted because we have to live with these numbers for the next 10 years. I will
  get together with our City Clerk and we will give a report on it together to see how
  we are doing and how much money we will be getting. To the family of Mr.
  Gondek he is an institution, a lot of knowledge and I know I met him 25 years
  ago, we went to Sacramento regarding the landfills. He will be greatly missed.
  To the Law Firm our condolences and to his family as well.
